subject: Close runway drift: ownership transfer and remediation playbook
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@atlashealth.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: AtlasHealth Procurement <procurement@atlashealth.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluation schedule — expected slip and next steps

Jonas / Laura,

Quick note from our side — we've got a scheduling conflict on the clinical ops team that will push our internal eval window by approximately 2–3 weeks. That means the target close date in the MAP will also slip unless we compress other milestones.

We understand these things happen. Can you send an updated MAP and a short remediation plan that shows:
- a re-baselined timeline with critical-path milestones
- fallback options if the clinical eval extends beyond the new window
- any prerequisites we need to unblock from procurement so we don't add delay on our side

Procurement has asked for an updated SOW/PO timeline to align budget cycles. If it's possible to present a short executive summary for their CFO this week, that would help.

Thanks,
Samantha
Samantha Lee
Head of Integrations, AtlasHealth
S: +1 (415) 555-0199

---
Attachments: (none referenced)
From: jonas.weber@redwood.com
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@atlashealth.com>, AtlasHealth Procurement <procurement@atlashealth.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 19 Oct 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluation schedule — proposed compact MAP and contingency

Samantha — thanks for the heads up and sorry to hear about the clinical ops conflict. I've attached a compact MAP (v2) that compresses non-critical milestones and introduces a canary evaluation for the most sensitive integration points. High level:

- Re-baseline: move final close date from 2027-11-15 to 2027-12-06 (three-week shift) with explicit checkpoints at 10/26, 11/09, 11/23.
- Contingency: If clinical eval extends beyond 11/23, we will run a parallel canary with a smaller dataset (2 clinics) to validate core path while clinical completes the full study.
- Procurement ask: to keep billing cycles aligned, we need a signed PO by 2027-11-02 or we risk slipping into the next budget window.

Action items (owner):
- Jonas: finalize exec-brief for CFO (draft attached) — due 10/21
- Laura: update risk log with quantified impact & mitigation (attachment forthcoming) — due 10/20
- Samantha/Procurement: confirm if PO by 11/02 is possible

I also included two fallback policies in the MAP: an accelerated integration sprint (adds 30% dev variance) and an SLA credit for two weeks of reduced throughput if the canary can't be completed. We can discuss which is preferable — the accelerated sprint increases engineering cost but shortens customer time-to-value.

Attachments: proposed-compact-MAP-v2.xlsx, exec-brief-draft.pdf

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
---
Attachment stubs: proposed-compact-MAP-v2.xlsx (XLSX, 48KB), exec-brief-draft.pdf (PDF, 120KB)
From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@atlashealth.com>
Date: Wed, 20 Oct 2027 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluation schedule — risk log update and escalation request

Looping in a short risk update and recommended escalation. I updated the internal risk log with two quantified entries:

1) Clinical ops schedule conflict (Likelihood: 60%, Impact: High) — Residual close delay = 2–3 weeks. Mitigation: canary evaluation + prioritized bug triage; residual cost = ~0.6 FTE-weeks of SRE/Eng.
2) Procurement timing (Likelihood: 30%, Impact: Medium) — If PO not approved by 11/02, contract will need to roll to next cycle; mitigation: CFO exec-brief + temporary invoice hold policy (works only with procurement approval).

Because the clinical risk has the highest impact, I recommend we escalate for an exception to grant a one-time SLA credit and commit an engineering burst if the customer approves the accelerated sprint. Request: Marissa — can you authorize a conditional credit (up to 2 weeks) and sign-off to allocate up to 0.6 FTE-weeks for SRE? If yes, I will add a formal remediation row to the MAP and notify the customer.

I've attached the risk-log CSV and a draft remediation matrix.

Attachments: risk-log-20271019.csv

Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
---
Attachment stubs: risk-log-20271019.csv (CSV, 12KB)
From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@atlashealth.com>, AtlasHealth Procurement <procurement@atlashealth.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Oct 2027 15:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluation schedule — remediation approved (conditional)

Thanks team — I reviewed the risk log and proposed MAP. Decision: approve conditional remediation with the following constraints:

- SLA credit: approve up to 2 weeks, but only if canary path fails to meet acceptance criteria after 11/23 review.
- Engineering burst: approve allocation of up to 0.6 FTE-weeks (SRE & Integration) to support canary and triage for priority defects.
- PO deadline: Procurement must confirm by 2027-11-02 for us to hold to the re-baselined close of 2027-12-06. If PO slips, update deal stage and notify GTM ops.

Jonas: finalize the exec-brief and include the conditional credit language and the acceptance criteria for the canary (I added notes in the draft). Laura: please add the remediation row to the MAP and include exact roll-back criteria.

I'll draft a short email to the customer summarizing commitments and next steps once you confirm updates. Keep the timeline tight — we do not want open-ended extensions.

Marissa Cole
VP Sales, Redwood Inference
